title: Week 5 Mastery Quiz — Early Africa, South Asia, East Asia, and the Americas

questions.prompt: Which evidence most directly supports a claim of deliberate urban planning?
choices: A later legend about a ruler
Standardized street layouts, drainage systems, and coordinated building patterns
A single imported bead
A modern map label
questions.explanation: Repeated, coordinated spatial features such as streets and drainage provide direct archaeological evidence of planning.

questions.prompt: Why is archaeology especially important for studying the Indus civilization?
choices: Its material remains are the only evidence from ancient South Asia.
Archaeologists can translate every surviving inscription.
Its script remains undeciphered, so material and spatial evidence carries particular importance.
Written royal biographies provide a complete political record.
questions.explanation: Because the Indus script remains undeciphered, archaeology is essential while many political and linguistic questions remain open.

questions.prompt: An oracle bone is best described as:
choices: an inscribed bone or shell used in Shang divination and studied as written evidence
a stone monument proving democratic government
a trade token from the Indus Valley
a Zhou law code defining the Mandate of Heaven
questions.explanation: Oracle bones are inscribed bones or shells associated with Shang divination and provide written evidence.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the Zhou concept later known as the Mandate of Heaven?
choices: A dynasty could never lose political legitimacy.
Legitimacy depended only on military conquest.
All rulers were selected by popular election.
Legitimate rule was connected to moral performance and could be forfeited.
questions.explanation: The Mandate of Heaven linked legitimate rule to moral performance and provided a framework for explaining dynastic change.

questions.prompt: Which inference from monumental architecture is most defensible?
choices: Large construction can indicate organized labor and important political, religious, or social priorities.
Every monument proves the existence of an absolute monarchy.
Monuments show that ordinary people agreed with elite priorities.
Similar monuments in two regions prove direct contact.
questions.explanation: Monuments can demonstrate organized resources and priorities, but they do not alone establish government type, consent, or diffusion.

choices: The independent invention of identical institutions everywhere
The spread of ideas, technologies, practices, or cultural traits through contact
The belief that geography determines political outcomes
The sequence of rulers from one lineage
questions.explanation: Cultural diffusion refers to cultural transmission through contact; it should be demonstrated with evidence rather than assumed from similarity.

questions.prompt: Two distant societies both build large ceremonial structures. What should a historian conclude first?
choices: One society copied the other.
Both societies had identical religions.
The similarity is an observation that requires additional evidence before claiming diffusion or shared origin.
Both societies were governed by kings.
questions.explanation: Similarity alone does not establish contact, copying, religion, or political structure.

questions.prompt: Which approach best avoids treating one civilization as the universal model?
choices: Rank societies by how closely they resemble Mesopotamia.
Assume writing is required for social complexity.
Use only societies with deciphered royal records.
Compare each society through its own evidence, environment, institutions, and historical pathway before making cross-regional claims.
questions.explanation: Context-first comparison allows meaningful similarities and differences without forcing all societies into one developmental template.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would most strongly support the existence of long-distance exchange?
choices: Materials at a site that can be securely traced to distant geological or production sources
A large local building
A story written thousands of years later
The existence of agriculture
questions.explanation: Provenanced nonlocal materials provide strong evidence that goods moved across distance.

choices: Every complex society developed the same institutions in the same order.
Complex societies emerged through multiple pathways, and different kinds of evidence reveal both similarities and important regional differences.
Archaeology can identify every ruler and law even without deciphered texts.
Political centralization is the only reliable measure of complexity.
questions.explanation: The week emphasizes multiple pathways to complexity and evidence-sensitive comparison across regions.

shortResponse.prompt: Using evidence from at least three regional cases, explain how early societies developed complex urban or political systems through different historical pathways. Include one limitation or uncertainty in the surviving evidence.
shortResponse.exemplar: Full-credit work makes a comparative claim, uses accurate evidence from at least three regional cases, explains similarities and differences rather than merely listing them, and acknowledges an evidentiary limitation or uncertainty.
